items.headline: Teachers' unions call island-wide strike on 30 Nov
items.summary: Several teachers' and principals' unions will hold a one-day national strike on 30 November, saying Budget 2027 failed to fix salary issues. The date is timed ahead of the 1 December debate on the Education Ministry's allocation.

items.headline: GMOA plans two-hour action on Monday
items.summary: Government doctors will step away from routine duties from noon to 2 PM on Monday, 23 November, to hold branch meetings over pay and allowance grievances left out of Budget 2027. Emergency services will continue.

items.headline: Third public sector pay rise due in January 2027
items.summary: PM Harini Amarasuriya told Parliament the third phase of salary increases for public servants and teachers will be paid from January 2027. A commission on salary and pension anomalies is due to report in July 2027.

items.headline: SJB MP questions Namal Rajapaksa's continued remand
items.summary: SJB MP Chithral Fernando argued in Parliament that the Bail Act makes bail the rule rather than the exception. He said he respected judicial independence but warned the precedent could affect MPs of any party.

items.headline: Two tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: British maritime monitors said two tankers were struck by unknown projectiles near Oman, with no casualties reported. Iran separately claimed a tanker caught fire after hitting a naval mine, which could not be verified.

items.headline: Opposition Leader objects to blocked Imran Khan debate
items.summary: Sajith Premadasa criticised the Speaker's rejection of an adjournment motion on former Pakistan PM Imran Khan, which was refused over concerns for ties with Pakistan. He also accused the Speaker of treating government and opposition MPs differently.

items.headline: First Budget 2027 expenditure heads approved
items.summary: On the first day of the committee stage, Parliament approved the 2027 allocations for the President's office, the Legislature and the Judiciary.

items.headline: Rs. 1.66 billion spent on stalled school projects
items.summary: The Committee on Public Accounts found that of 72 education projects started in 2018–2021, only 35 are complete and 20 are stalled over contract disputes. It also reviewed a dropped plan for three national schools per division.

items.headline: Vehicle import taxes reviewed by committee
items.summary: Parliament's Ways and Means Committee discussed with Customs how to simplify vehicle import taxes, EV incentives and clearance delays. No immediate tax changes were announced.
